content: Within this chamber, a substance capable of absorbing carbon dioxide released during respiration is included. Commonly used substances for this purpose are soda lime pellets or cotton wads soaked in potassium hydroxide. The device is connected to a thin glass U-tube filled with a manometric fluid. When the organism consumes oxygen, it simultaneously produces an equivalent volume of carbon dioxide. This control respirometer contains either a non-living specimen or an object of equivalent mass to the living organism.
